guide.title: Korean BBQ in Queens: 149th Place, Downtown Flushing, Northern Boulevard East and Beyond
guide.intro: Korean barbecue in Queens is cooked on a grill at the diner's own table, and nineteen rooms in the borough work that way. Eight of them stand in Murray Hill, on and around 149th Place, where the street numbers run 40-03, 40-07, 40-09, 40-11 and 41-06 along one block. Six more follow Northern Boulevard east through Auburndale, Bayside, Oakland Gardens and Douglaston, and one sits on Roosevelt Avenue in downtown Flushing. The last four are scattered west and south, in Astoria, Rego Park, Long Island City and Howard Beach. Charcoal burns at Hahm Ji Bach, Mapo BBQ, San Soo Kap San, Daori BBQ, Yuk Jun Gui and Jongro BBQ; Han Joo cooks on a clear crystal slab over a gas flame; and Tong Sam Gyup Goo Yi in Auburndale uses a domed cast-iron sottukong.

sections.heading: 149th Place and 41st Avenue, Murray Hill
sections.body:
Eight of the nineteen stand within one block of each other in Murray Hill, on 149th Place and the streets that cross it.

On 149th Place the street numbers run in sequence: Daori BBQ at 40-03, New Kum Sung BBQ at 40-07, Goo Gong Tan at 40-09, Hahm Ji Bach at 40-11 and Han Joo BBQ at 41-06. Daori grills duck over charcoal at the table, under overhead vents. New Kum Sung sets a flat grill on every table and the pork caramelizes on the tabletop grate. Goo Gong Tan lays whole clams on the slats of the grill at the table, where they open over the heat. At Hahm Ji Bach a server carries a bucket of glowing coals to the grill at the table and slabs of pork belly go on above it. Han Joo cooks on a slab of clear crystal set over a gas flame at the table, tilted so the fat runs off into a basin of kimchi.

Three more sit on the streets around that row. Mapo BBQ is at 149-24 41st Avenue, where the same bucket of coals goes under the grill at the table and galbi and black pork cook over the embers. Yuk Jun Gui is at 41-05 150th Street, where the charcoal grill is set up at the table and grilled eel is the specialty. Golden Pig is at 152-12 Northern Boulevard, where short ribs, pork belly and vegetables are grilled at the table on a pork and wagyu menu.

sections.heading: Roosevelt Avenue, Downtown Flushing
sections.body:
Downtown Flushing carries one room of this kind, and it sits on Roosevelt Avenue rather than on the 149th Place row.

Jongro BBQ is at 155-14 Roosevelt Avenue. Charcoal is the fuel, the meat is grilled at the table under overhead smoke lamps, and laser thermometers are used to read the heat. A room under the same name trades at 22 West 32nd Street in Manhattan's Koreatown, and the Flushing room runs the same charcoal service.

sections.heading: Northern Boulevard east: Auburndale to Douglaston
sections.body:
Six stand along the eastern run of Northern Boulevard and the streets off it, from Auburndale out to Douglaston.

San Soo Kap San is at 171-04 Northern Boulevard in Auburndale, and its own site states that the barbecue is served on a charcoal grill built into the table. Tong Sam Gyup Goo Yi is at 162-23 Depot Road in the same neighborhood, where the grill in the table is a black cast-iron dome with a tapered handle and stripes of pork belly cook down its sides with the heat turned high.

Bayside carries two. Won KBBQ, which also trades as O2 BBQ, is at 45-53 Bell Boulevard, a room of table grills and television screens where the servers cook the meat at the table on an all-you-can-eat service. Blacksmith BBQ is at 43-30 Corporal Kennedy Street, where the all-you-can-eat service is built around the grill at each table.

Bi Won is in unit 1 at 61-58 Springfield Boulevard in Oakland Gardens, and its own site describes Meongsuk Galbi grilled at the table. Sungbookdong BBQ is at 248-25 Northern Boulevard in Douglaston, at the eastern edge of the borough, where a menu listing states that there is a grill at every table.

sections.heading: Off the belt: Astoria, Rego Park, Long Island City and Howard Beach
sections.body:
Four stand away from the Flushing and Northern Boulevard corridors, in four separate neighborhoods of western and southern Queens.

Prime No. 7 is at 34-19 Steinway Street in Astoria, where a Korean grill sits at the table for the cooking and sushi runs alongside the barbecue; it opened in September 2025 and its all-you-can-eat service tops out at $55. Iron Age Korean Steakhouse is at 61-35 Junction Boulevard in Rego Park, the Rego Center address, where diners grill their own meat at the table with staff on hand to help with the cooking.

Wonderpig KBBQ is at 37-08 Queens Boulevard in Long Island City, and its own site offers tabletop grilling or chef-prepared dishes. KPOT Korean BBQ and Hot Pot is at 161-53 Cross Bay Boulevard in Howard Beach, where a grill is set into every table alongside a hot-pot burner and the meat is cooked on the grill half.

faq.question: What is tabletop Korean BBQ, and what counts as one?
faq.answer: Tabletop Korean barbecue means the grill is set into the diner's own table and the meat is cooked there, whether the party grills it or a server does. A charcoal grate, a gas flame under a clear crystal slab, a domed cast-iron sottukong and a combined grill and hot-pot burner all count. A soondubu house, a fried-chicken house, a gukbap or jajangmyeon house, and a kitchen that grills the meat and sends it out already cooked all fail that definition, however Korean the menu is. Gyu-Kaku at 40-52 Main Street in Flushing has grills set into its tables and is a Japanese yakiniku house, so the format is met and the cuisine is not.

faq.question: Where in Queens are the tabletop grills concentrated?
faq.answer: Eight of the nineteen stand in Murray Hill on and around 149th Place, at street numbers 40-03, 40-07, 40-09, 40-11 and 41-06 on 149th Place itself, with Mapo BBQ at 149-24 41st Avenue, Yuk Jun Gui at 41-05 150th Street and Golden Pig at 152-12 Northern Boulevard. Six more follow Northern Boulevard east through Auburndale, Bayside, Oakland Gardens and Douglaston. One, Jongro BBQ, is on Roosevelt Avenue in downtown Flushing. The remaining four are in Astoria, Rego Park, Long Island City and Howard Beach.

faq.question: Which rooms burn charcoal rather than gas?
faq.answer: San Soo Kap San at 171-04 Northern Boulevard states on its own site that the barbecue is served on a charcoal grill built into the table. Hahm Ji Bach at 40-11 149th Place and Mapo BBQ at 149-24 41st Avenue both have a server carry a bucket of glowing coals to the grill at the table. Yuk Jun Gui at 41-05 150th Street sets a charcoal grill up at the table, and Daori BBQ at 40-03 149th Place grills its duck over charcoal at the table under overhead vents. Jongro BBQ at 155-14 Roosevelt Avenue runs a charcoal service under overhead smoke lamps. Han Joo BBQ at 41-06 149th Place is the gas counterpart, with a clear crystal slab over a gas flame at the table.

faq.question: What are the opening hours?
faq.answer: No source states the opening hours of twelve of these nineteen restaurants, so none are given for them here. Seven publish theirs. Yuk Jun Gui lists 11am to 11pm Tuesday through Sunday and closed on Monday. Golden Pig lists 11:30am to midnight Monday through Friday and noon to midnight at the weekend. Won KBBQ lists 11:30am to midnight Sunday through Thursday and 11:30am to 1am on Friday and Saturday, and Blacksmith BBQ lists 11:30am to 1am Sunday through Thursday and 11:30am to 2am on Friday and Saturday. Prime No. 7 lists 11:40am to midnight Sunday through Thursday and 11:40am to 1am on Friday and Saturday. Wonderpig KBBQ lists noon to 10pm Monday through Thursday, noon to midnight on Friday and Saturday, and noon to 11pm on Sunday. Iron Age Korean Steakhouse lists 11am to 10:30pm.

faq.question: Is Murray Hill in Queens the same place as Murray Hill in Manhattan?
faq.answer: No. They are two neighborhoods that share a name. The Queens one sits around 149th Place and 41st Avenue on the east side of Flushing, and eight of the nineteen stand there. The Manhattan one sits around Park Avenue and East 36th Street. Auburndale, Oakland Gardens and Howard Beach, which carry four more of the nineteen between them, are likewise Queens neighborhoods rather than separate municipalities.

photos.title: Roosevelt Avenue at Union Street, downtown Flushing, Queens
photos.description: Looking east along Roosevelt Avenue from the corner of Union Street on a wet afternoon, with a low row of shopfronts and stacked storefront signs running down the block and a pale tower rising behind them. Cars and a bus fill the roadway and pedestrians with umbrellas cross the sidewalk in the foreground.

places.name: Hahm Ji Bach
places.summary: Hahm Ji Bach is at 40-11 149th Place in Murray Hill. A server carries a bucket of glowing coals to the grill at the table, and thick slabs of pork belly are grilled above it.

places.name: New Kum Sung BBQ
places.summary: New Kum Sung BBQ is at 40-07 149th Place in Murray Hill. Big flat grills sit on every table, and the meat crisps and caramelizes on the tabletop grate.
places.history: The dining room is described as modestly sized.

places.name: Mapo BBQ
places.summary: Mapo BBQ is at 149-24 41st Avenue in Murray Hill. A server sets a bucket of glowing coals under the grill at the table, and cuts of galbi and black pork sizzle over the crackling embers.

places.name: San Soo Kap San
places.summary: San Soo Kap San is at 171-04 Northern Boulevard in Auburndale. The restaurant's own site states that the barbecue is served on a charcoal grill built into the table.
places.history: An earlier address at 38-13 Union Street still appears on the restaurant's own site. That address is now occupied by Hangukgwan, a separate business.

places.name: Han Joo BBQ
places.summary: Han Joo BBQ is at 41-06 149th Place in Murray Hill. A slab of clear, glistening crystal set over a gas flame serves as the grill at the table, angled so the fat from the pork belly runs off into a basin of kimchi.
places.history: The restaurant also trades as Han Joo Chik Naeng Myun & BBQ, naming the cold noodles it serves alongside the barbecue.

places.name: Daori BBQ
places.summary: Daori BBQ is at 40-03 149th Place in Murray Hill, and duck is what it grills. Staff cook the sliced duck over charcoal on the grill at the table, in a room of stone-plate grills and overhead vents.

places.name: Goo Gong Tan
places.summary: Goo Gong Tan is in unit 1 at 40-09 149th Place in Murray Hill. Whole clams are laid on the slats of the grill at the table, where they slowly open over the heat, and pork belly goes on the same grate.
places.history: The house takes shellfish as its specialty and extends the barbecue format to it.

places.name: Yuk Jun Gui
places.summary: Yuk Jun Gui is at 41-05 150th Street in Murray Hill. The charcoal grill is set up at the table, and the tables are small enough that the grill and the side dishes compete for room.
places.history: Grilled eel is the specialty, alongside the barbecue classics. The restaurant lists hours of 11am to 11pm Tuesday through Sunday, and closed on Monday.

places.name: Tong Sam Gyup Goo Yi
places.summary: Tong Sam Gyup Goo Yi is at 162-23 Depot Road in Auburndale. The grill in the table is a gleaming black cast-iron dome with a tapered handle, and stripes of pork belly cook down its sides with the heat turned high.
places.history: The domed cast-iron pan is the sottukong format. The New York Times reviewed the restaurant in September 2016.

places.name: Bi Won
places.summary: Bi Won is in unit 1 at 61-58 Springfield Boulevard in Oakland Gardens. The restaurant's own site describes its Meongsuk Galbi, a beef short rib, as grilled at the table.
places.history: The address takes a Bayside mailing designation; Oakland Gardens is a neighborhood of its own.

places.name: Golden Pig
places.summary: Golden Pig is at 152-12 Northern Boulevard in Murray Hill. Marinated short ribs, pork belly and assorted vegetables are grilled at the table, and the operator's own site frames the meal as a shared table rather than a plate of meat.
places.history: The menu runs to pork and wagyu. The restaurant lists hours of 11:30am to midnight Monday through Friday, and noon to midnight on Saturday and Sunday.

places.name: KPOT Korean BBQ and Hot Pot
places.address: 161-53 Cross Bay Boulevard, Howard Beach, NY 11414
places.summary: KPOT Korean BBQ and Hot Pot is at 161-53 Cross Bay Boulevard in Howard Beach. A grill is set into every table alongside a hot-pot burner, and diners cook their own meat on the grill half.
places.history: The chain runs two further New York City rooms, at 430 Albee Square West in Downtown Brooklyn and at 1217 Surf Avenue in Coney Island. All-you-can-eat is the pricing model.

links.note: Jongro BBQ is at 155-14 Roosevelt Avenue in downtown Flushing, where it burns charcoal under the grill at the table.
Won KBBQ on Bell Boulevard and Blacksmith BBQ on Corporal Kennedy Street are Bayside places.
KPOT's two Brooklyn rooms, at 430 Albee Square West and 1217 Surf Avenue, are the same chain as the Howard Beach one.
Iron Age Korean Steakhouse runs the Junction Boulevard room in Rego Park and one at 1265 North Milwaukee Avenue in Wicker Park.
